 Live Trump Asia trip live updates: Trump greets Putin, Xi as APEC summit begins 
 Trump will participate this week in a trilateral meeting with Putin and Xi. 
 1:32 China's President Xi Jinping watches as President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin shake hands before the welcome banquet at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, China, Nov. 18, 2026. Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press via AP By ABC NEWS Last Updated: November 18, 2026, 1:39 PM EST 
 President Donald Trump is traveling to Asia for meetings with global leaders and for his second visit to China for a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.
 ABC News will have special coverage of the Trump-Xi-Putin meeting led by "World News Tonight" anchor David Muir, who will be anchoring from Shenzhen, China, across programs and platforms.
 Muir will anchor "World News Tonight" from China on Wednesday, Nov. 18 and Thursday, Nov. 19.
 Chief White House correspondent Mary Bruce and White House correspondent Karen Travers will also be reporting from China.
 See the most recent developments below.
 Key Headlines
 2 hours and 48 minutes ago White House releases details on agreements with Philippines, Thailand 
 8:47 AM EST Trump and Putin to hold bilateral meeting on Thursday, US official confirms 
 7:12 AM EST Trump and Putin shake hands as APEC summit begins 
 4:57 AM EST Trump personally greeted by Xi in surprise gesture upon arrival to Shenzhen 
 Here's how the news is developing. 2 hours and 48 minutes ago 
 White House releases details on agreements with Philippines, Thailand 
 The White House released details on agreements reached during President Trump's visit to Manila, claiming to have secured more than $17 billion "in commercial deals and strategic investments for U.S. companies."
 According to a fact sheet released by the White House, a $12 billion sale with Philippine Airlines was finalized, with the airline expected to purchase up to 20 Boeing 787 aircrafts and GE Aerospace engines.
 The U.S. will also provide more than $2 billion in a loan package to boost Philippine defense and security capabilities from U.S. suppliers, according to the fact sheet.
 President Donald Trump and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. shake hands at Malacanang Presidential Palace on November 18, 2026, in Manila, Philippines. Carlos Barria/Reuters The White House said that once the trade deal with Thailand is signed, it will "eliminate tariffs on 99 percent of goods and remove non-tariff barriers on American vehicles, medical devices, pharmaceuticals, ethanol, and poultry."
 "Separately, Thailand intends to commit up to $123 million toward the purchase of America’s High Mobility Artillery Rocket Systems (HIMARS)," the fact sheet added.
 -ABC News' Emily Chang 
 8:47 AM EST 
 Trump and Putin to hold bilateral meeting on Thursday, US official confirms 
 President Donald Trump will participate in a one-on-one meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday, a U.S. official confirmed to ABC.
 The official did not immediately provide a scheduled time for the meeting. A one-on-one meeting had not previously been on Trump's schedule, with a senior U.S. official telling reporters last week that "there’s no bilateral scheduled" between the two.
 Trump on Tuesday expressed openness to a potential bilateral meeting with his Russian counterpart, saying, "I would if it’s available. I would do that."
 -ABC News' Emily Chang 
 7:12 AM EST 
 Trump and Putin shake hands as APEC summit begins 
 President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin greeted each other with a handshake on Wednesday as Chinese President Xi Jinping looked on.
 President Donald Trump prepares to shake hands with Russian President Vladimir Putin as China's President Xi Jinping looks on before the welcome banquet at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen on Nov. 18, 2026. Iori Sagisawa/POOL/AFP via Getty Images The greeting came as a wider group of APEC leaders gathered for a group photo before a welcome banquet. The American, Chinese and Russian leaders are scheduled to hold a meeting on Thursday.
 Putin on Wednesday said he sees "substantial potential benefit" in gatherings such as the APEC summit and the trilateral , which will take place on the gathering's sidelines.
 China's President Xi Jinping watches as President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin shake hands before the welcome banquet at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, China, Nov. 18, 2026. Iori Sagisawa/Kyodo News/Pool via AP Putin said such meetings allow for leaders to "sit at the same table, exchange views, resolve differences between states -- whether political, economic or security-related -- by seeking compromise and balancing interests," according to the text of his remarks published by his office.
 Xi earlier said he looked forward to an exchange of views with Trump on major issues, including China-U.S. relations and Asia-Pacific cooperation, according to China's Xinhua News Agency.
 -ABC News’ Joe Simonetti and Kevin Shalvey 
 4:57 AM EST 
 Trump personally greeted by Xi in surprise gesture upon arrival to Shenzhen 
 In a surprise move, President Donald Trump was personally greeted by Chinese President Xi Jinping at the foot of Air Force One on Wednesday after the American president arrived in Shenzhen, China.
 The Chinese president rolled out the red carpet and displayed pomp and circumstance complete with troops marching and dozens of enthusiastic dancers.
 President Donald Trump walks down the stairs of Air Force One as China's President Xi Jinping waits at the bottom as he arrives at Shenzhen Baoan International Airport to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Summit in Shenzhen, in China's southern Guangdong Province, on Nov 18, 2026. Mandel Ngan/POOL/AFP via Getty Images Xi emerged from his vehicle and walked down the red carpet to meet Trump at the bottom of the stairs, a shocking appearance from the Chinese president that was not expected. Xi did not greet Trump personally at the airport back in May when the president visited Beijing.
 The move comes after Trump himself broke from protocol and greeted Xi on the tarmac at Joint Base Andrews during Xi's state visit to Washington in September.
 Trump fist-pumped upon emerging from the Qatar-gifted Air Force One as a crowd in pink and blue outfits holding poms-poms chanted "warm welcome" in Mandarin, according to a pool reporter on the ground.
 According to the pool, the arrival ceremony participants also included Chinese first lady Peng Liyuan, U.S. Ambassador to China David Perdue and his wife, Consul General Pauline Kao, along with China’s Executive Vice Minister of Foreign Affairs H.E. MA Zhaoxu and Ambassador of the People’s Republic of China to the United States H.E. XIE Feng.
 President Donald Trump walks with China's President Xi Jinping after arriving at Shenzhen Baoan International Airport to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, in China's southern Guangdong Province, on Nov. 18, 2026. Mandel Ngan/POOL/AFP via Getty Images The leaders stood side-by-side as the American national anthem played, with Trump standing at a salute for the song. After the Chinese anthem was played, there was a military flyover of five jets, which left plumes of red, blue and yellow, according to the pool reporter traveling with the president. Trump and Xi then made their way down the red carpet, before Trump entered his motorcade.
 After 24 hours in Manila, Philippines, Trump landed in Shenzhen for the APEC summit, which starts on Wednesday, and his high-stakes meetings with Xi and Russia’s Vladimir Putin, which is scheduled for Thursday.
 -ABC N ews' Michelle Stoddart, Emily Cha n g a n d Fritz Farrow
